problems.stem: A planar truss has 11 members and 7 joints. Based on the count test, how is it classified?
problems.explanation: Because 2j - 3 = 2(7) - 3 = 11, the member count is consistent with a statically determinate planar truss.

problems.stem: How many members are required for a simple planar truss with 8 joints to satisfy m = 2j - 3?
At an unloaded joint with two non-collinear members only, what can you conclude?
options: Both members must be in compression
One member is in tension and one in compression
problems.explanation: If there is no external load or support reaction at that joint, both non-collinear member forces must be zero for equilibrium.

problems.stem: Why are ideal truss members often treated as two-force members?
options: Because loads act only at joints and pin connections prevent moment transfer in the ideal model
Because truss members can never go into compression
Because all truss members are vertical
Because member weight is always zero in reality
problems.explanation: In the ideal truss model, joint loading and pin connections mean each member carries axial force only.
